trust_decision.summary: The proxy decides whether a caller may choose the outbound destination (URL-valued model/file_id, api_base and observability hosts in body or metadata) and whether admin-configured credentials may follow a caller-chosen destination. It decides this at auth time in is_request_body_safe, in add_litellm_data_to_request via _reject_url_valued_destinations, and in the router's credential-clearing step.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'unvalidated request-body routing parameters' and 'SSRF', which points to the central URL-valued model/file_id guard and its caller add_litellm_data_to_request; is_request_body_safe (litellm/proxy/auth/auth_utils.py:406) is the second obvious place to look.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Test Connection on a configured model (name plus stored credential, no own connection fields) must still inherit the config credentials, and an add-model request carrying its own api_base plus api_key must test as sent. The allow_client_side_credentials opt-in must restore inheritance. Benign bracket metadata (litellm_metadata[tags], [spend_logs_metadata][owner]) must pass. Ordinary Azure deployment path names (dall-e-3) must route. Allowlisted hosts in provider_url_destination_allowed_hosts must pass. An over-broad fix (dropping config credentials always, rejecting any bracket key, rejecting any '/' in the path model) breaks these.
